definitions_cited.tolerance: 0.35 percentage points between the custodian gross return (custodian time-weighted return grossed up by fees over the daily-mean served value, the ~35 v2 construction) and the restated served return; TOL_PP = 0.35 in the same scripts; UNCLASSED_90.json method.return_test
definitions_cited.dollars_tie: each of the four items (beginning value, ending value, net additions, net gains) ties within max(1 dollar, 0.1 percent of the larger): UNCLASSED_90.json method.dollar_tie
definitions_cited.flow_days_tie: the set of days on which the custodian transaction rows carry an external flow (by return date, day sums above half a cent) equals the set of served flow days: as ~120 x1_crosstab.py dates_same; CONTESTED_51.json date_sets_ledger_vs_served
definitions_cited.what_dollars_and_flow_days_tying_means_h: the four aggregates tie and the day SETS are equal. It does not require each day's amount to reproduce; that stronger test (234 of 235 flow days, 50 of 51 segments, DB-b-142 as quoted in CONTESTED_51_MEANING.json) is reported, not made a condition. The one segment with a day that does not reproduce carries an administrative expense row; under either reading it stays RECONCILES_YES and TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED (both START and MID close).

axes.name: RECONCILES
axes.question: Does the segment's return close against the other system's, with its dollars and flow days tying?
axes.domain: tie-out segments whose dollars and flow days were read on both sides

value_meaning.RECONCILES_YES: the return closes within 0.35 pp under at least one of START, MID, END; AND the four dollar items tie; AND the flow-day sets are equal
value_meaning.RECONCILES_NO: the segment is in the domain and at least one of those three conditions fails

axes.consumer_rule: a consumer rejects any RECONCILES_* row whose reconciles_claim is not measured
axes.domain_membership_rule: a segment is in the domain when a two-sided dollar read (custodian point for the range against the served daily series) and a flow-day comparison exist for it; today that is the 90 segments of worker 108's table

axes.name: TIMING
axes.question: Which flow timing did the other system use?

value_meaning.TIMING_START: exactly one admitted timing closes and it is START
value_meaning.TIMING_MID: exactly one admitted timing closes and it is MID
value_meaning.TIMING_END: exactly one admitted timing closes and it is END (no member today: END closes in 0 of the 51)
value_meaning.TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED: more than one admitted timing closes; the data cannot say, and that is the final answer for the segment, not a contest and not a class of disagreement

axes.claim_reason: a fit is evidence and not the custodian's statement (ruling), so the three named timings are inferred; TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED states a measured count (two or more timings close) and asserts no timing
axes.consumer_rule: a consumer rejects a TIMING_START, TIMING_MID or TIMING_END row whose timing_claim is not inferred, and never reads TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED as a timing

mece.finding: MECE over each declared domain, by subtraction from the printed denominators, with 0 uncovered. 244 = 90 in the RECONCILES domain + 154 outside it. 90 = 51 RECONCILES_YES + 39 RECONCILES_NO. 51 = 4 (exactly one timing closes: TIMING_START 3, TIMING_MID 1, TIMING_END 0) + 47 TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED. Inside the TIMING domain the count of closing timings is 1, 2 or 3 (RECONCILES_YES requires at least 1), so 'exactly one' (three values, one per admitted timing) and 'more than one' (one value) leave nothing over. The 185 classed: 154 are outside the RECONCILES domain (no two-sided dollar read exists for them: their classes were set from event-date and day-count tests, UNEXPLAINED_244.json classes) and 31 (the accrual class) are RECONCILES_NO. The 8 unclassed are RECONCILES_NO. On the TIMING axis none of the 185, 8 or 39 applies (outside the domain: TIMING is asked only of segments that reconcile).
mece.evidence: y1_place.py output (counts only): domain 90 = {51, 31, 8}; four dollar items tie 51 / 0 / 0; flow-day sets equal 51 / 30 / 8; RECONCILES rule met 51 / 0 / 0; closing timings START 50, MID 48, END 0 of 51; set of closing timings START+MID 47, START 3, MID 1. same_grain.finding: Every value is a property of ONE segment, the (account, start, end) range that is the 244 and the 90 and the 51. RECONCILES is one segment's return against one custodian point plus its own four items and day set; TIMING is read from the same segment's three restated returns. No value is a property of an account (86 accounts hold the 90 segments, so an account value would mix grains), of a flow day, or of a pool: the pooled median log ratio over 86 flow days in CONTESTED_51.json is a pool-level figure and is deliberately NOT used to place any segment.
same_grain.evidence: each placement in y1_place.py is computed per row of table90.pkl (90 rows); 90 rows, 90 placements; the earlier record states the pooled figure 'is not a segment-level fact' (CONTESTED_51.json measurements.pooled_median_log_ratio_implied_day_return_to_account_noise.reading).

intent_coherence.finding: One axis, one intent. RECONCILES asks only whether the number ties and is measured; TIMING asks only which convention produced it and is inferred. No RECONCILES value says anything about timing and no TIMING value says anything about whether the segment ties: TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED is not RECONCILES_NO (47 of 51 reconcile and cannot be timed), and RECONCILES_NO carries no timing. The label CONTESTED today mixes the two intents: it names a disagreement (the return does or does not tie) for segments whose only open question is a fact no record can state (the time of day), which is the break this proposal separates.
intent_coherence.evidence: CTO msg 5835 item 1 'only one is a disagreement'; CONTESTED_51_MEANING.json what_is_settled_for_all_51 / what_is_not_settled_for_all_51 (all four dollar items tie in 51 of 51, flow days tie in 51 of 51, the open item is the time of day).

state_coherence.finding: Which values one remedy does NOT move. (1) A custodian statement of its flow-timing convention moves TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED (47) to a stated timing and changes its claim; it moves no RECONCILES value, and it leaves the 4 inferred values to be confirmed or contradicted, not re-measured. (2) A change of tolerance or of the return construction (fee base) can move a segment between RECONCILES_YES and RECONCILES_NO and between TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED and a single timing; it is the one remedy that moves both axes, and it is a ruling, not an observation. (3) A ruling that accrual-explained dollar gaps count as tying moves the 31 accrual-class segments from RECONCILES_NO toward RECONCILES_YES and into the TIMING domain; this proposal does not make it. (4) The shared code table's class for the one expense row (cell DB-b-146) moves no value on either axis, because that segment is RECONCILES_YES and TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED under either reading. (5) Reading more of the 154 (a two-sided dollar read) moves segments INTO the RECONCILES domain; it moves no segment already placed. (6) Re-timing the 4 inferred values requires a segment-level read of the custodian's intraday series, which no record read shows.
state_coherence.evidence: CONTESTED_51_MEANING.json groups 1, 3, 4, 5 (what_would_close_it per group) and not_established; UNCLASSED_90.json classes (accrual rule; 13 of the 31 close with accrual scaling under END, 18 only under START or MID, quoted not re-derived); y1_place.py gap figures: START and MID both within tolerance in 47 of 47 NOT_DETERMINED.
